item.title: Case Keenum was ready to quit playing football until Ben Johnson called
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Case Keenum spent the entire 2024 season on the Texans' injured reserve list with a foot injury, and when his contract expired at the end of that year, he figured his football career had come to an end.
item.content:encoded:
Case Keenum spent the entire 2024 season on the Texans' injured reserve list with a foot injury, and when his contract expired at the end of that year, he figured his football career had come to an end. Then Ben Johnson called.

Johnson had just become head coach of the Bears and knew he had a young franchise quarterback in Caleb Williams and a promising young backup in Tyson Bagent, but Johnson also wanted to add a veteran to the quarterback room, and Keenum was his choice. Keenum said on Pardon My Take that one conversation with Johnson was all he needed to realize he still wanted to play football.

"I was basically ready to call it quits and be done playing football, and Ben calls me," Keenum said. "I'm in Hawaii at the NFLPA event and I get a call from Ben Johnson. He said, You still want to come play? I was like, Let's meet and talk about it. We met for what was supposed to be 15 minutes, and two and a half hours later I was like, Where do I sign? Let's freakin' do this. I'm ready to run through a brick wall for that man."

Keenum said he was amazed to discover how similar he and Johnson are in the way they see the game. So he signed and hasn't regretted it for a minute.

"It got me geeked up, excited, really helped me spark that love of football again, and it's been a magical year and a half," Keenum said. "It's a special group of guys, Ben's a special man, and I'm just happy to be along for the ride."

The 38-year-old Keenum was more than just along for the ride on Monday night, when he played his first game in a Bears uniform and played very well in leading them to a win over the Eagles. Keenum has been glad every day that Johnson kept his career going, and now Johnson is very glad he added that veteran to his quarterback room.

item.title: Wink Martindale offers to help "outclassed" Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Coaching inexperience is holding the Cowboys back.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys' failure to beat the Ravens in Rio came from all three phases of the team. The offense failed to turn first and goal from the two with 20 seconds left into a game-winning touchdown, the special teams served up favorable field position on the kickoff after the game-tying field goal, and the defense allowed the Ravens to gain enough yards to set up the game-winning field goal.

The ultimate blame resides with coach Brian Schottenheimer, who shouldn't be learning the job of being an effective head coach while on the job.

Still, the defense continues to be a problem. Long-time NFL and college defensive coach Wink Martindale spoke bluntly about the situation during his latest appearance on Talkin' Ball with Pat Leonard.

"I don't want to be an asshole but he’s being outclassed right now," Martindale said regarding Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker. "So Jerry [Jones] can call me and I'll go help him. But, you know, I'm talking about helping the coordinator."

Matching a head coach who is learning the job on the fly with a defensive coordinator who is learning the job on the fly isn't ideal. It would have been useful for Schottenheimer, who has no former NFL head coaches on his staff, to have access to a key lieutenant who has done the job of head coach before — and whose experiences can help Schottenheimer realize the right answers to the test before he turns the paperwork in.

That's really the problem with the Cowboys. They lack the ability to prepare for the unique situations that experienced coaches know how to address. It played out on Sunday, giving the Cowboys a loss that could echo into January

And that could be the difference between making it to the playoffs or going home after Week 18, for the third straight season.

item.content:encoded:
Tampa Bay has announced a series of roster moves on Wednesday morning.

The Buccaneers have placed receiver Jalen McMillan on injured reserve after he suffered a knee injury during Sunday’s loss to the Vikings. McMillan is reportedly expected to be out for 6-to-8 weeks.

After catching 37 passes for 461 yards with eight touchdowns as a rookie in 2024, McMillan has been limited to just six games over the last two seasons due to injury.

Additionally, Tampa Bay announced the previously reported moves of signing safety Ifeatu Melifonwu to the 53-man roster off of the club’s practice squad and signing quarterback Brett Rypien to the practice squad.

Jalon Daniels is expected to start at QB with Baker Mayfield sidelined for at least three weeks with a dislocated right thumb. Rypien joins Easton Stick on the practice squad.

item.title: UFL shuffles head coaches (and rosters) after relocation of teams
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The UFL's status as a single company with eight offices sprinkled throughout the country gives the spring league plenty of flexibility when it comes to moving the pieces on the chessboard.
item.content:encoded:
The UFL's status as a single company with eight offices sprinkled throughout the country gives the spring league plenty of flexibility when it comes to moving the pieces on the chessboard.

Most recently, the relocation of two franchises from Birmingham and Houston to Rhode Island and Colorado, respectively, has prompted the shuffling of three head coaches.

Last year, local Alabama legend A.J. McCarron became the head coach of the Birmingham Stallions. He'll now be moving to Pawtucket. Which sounds more like the premise of a bad sitcom. He'll be joined by the Birmingham roster.

Rick Neuheisel, who had coached the Dallas Renegades (a team that will continue to exist), transfers to the Colorado branch. Which brings the former Buffaloes head coach back to the area where his coaching career first flourished.

So what about the Renegades? Former Houston Gamblers coach Kevin Sumlin will take over the team in Dallas.

And here's the last big twist. The Renegades roster will move to Colorado with Neuheisel. Which means that, even though the Houston franchise was dumped for a team in Colorado, the Renegades are the team making the Browns-Ravens transmogrification. And the Gamblers will become the new Renegades.

So, basically, Houston moved to Dallas and Dallas moved to Colorado and Birmingham moved to Rhode Island and that's how it will be until the next time the UFL reshuffles the deck.

item.title: Amazon extends Kirk Herbstreit, with a significant caveat
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Kirk Herbstreit claims he's oblivious to American politics.
item.content:encoded:
Kirk Herbstreit claims he's oblivious to American politics. He's also not up to speed on corporate politics.

Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reports that Amazon Prime Video and Herbstreit have agreed to an extension that would keep him in the Thursday Night Football booth beyond the 2026 season. But there's a catch.

A big one.

Per Marchand, Amazon has retained the ability to cut the cord with Herbstreit in the event that it can land someone else.

Basically, Herbstreit has become Amazon's bird in the hand. He's the leverage for the contract talks with whomever Amazon will target for the seat.

Amazon wanted Rams coach Sean McVay in early 2022. McVay, whose team had just won the Super Bowl, opted not to walk off into the sunset with a brand-new Lombardi Trophy for a $20 million per year TV gig. After a disappointing 2022 season, McVay's position changed — but it was too late. The seat was filled by Herbstreit.

This new deal apparently allows Amazon to take a year-to-year approach with Herbstreit. Prime Video can pursue McVay or Travis Kelce or Troy Aikman or Greg Olsen or anyone else whose attention isn't divided between pro and college football.

Then again, there's a chance Herbstreit will be all-in with the NFL come 2027. He's in the final year of his ESPN contract, too. Per Marchand, ESPN plans to wait to address Herbstreit's situation after college football season ends.

So, basically, the guy with a full-time college job and a full-time NFL job could end up with both, one, or none by 2027. If nothing else, a reduction in his workload would give him more time to understand why folks would be inclined to boo Ted Cruz.

item.title: Josh Allen remains the MVP favorite, but Brock Purdy is lurking
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Even with no touchdown passes and a pair of interceptions on Sunday against the Chargers, Bills quarterback Josh Allen remains the clear MVP favorite.
item.content:encoded:
Even with no touchdown passes and a pair of interceptions on Sunday against the Chargers, Bills quarterback Josh Allen remains the clear MVP favorite.

His Week 3 performance actually improved his odds.

Allen has gone from +500 to +260 to win his second NFL MVP award. Behind him currently is 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy, at +425.

Purdy deserves to be high on the list. The 49ers are 3-0, and Purdy has an off-the-charts passer rating of 133.1. He has nine touchdown passes on only 83 attempts, with one interception. He's averaging 9.5 yards per attempt. Purdy also has 93 rushing yards and a touchdown.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is currently +600, and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes sits at +800. Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is at +850, and Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence has odds of +1000.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who was initially off the board after his hamstring injury, is buried in the field at +5500. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, who came in second a year ago for the MVP award, is at +8000.

Last year's winner, Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, currently has odds of +2800.

item.title: Jayden Daniels will be a limited participant in practice
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Quarterback Jayden Daniels made the trip to London with the Commanders for this week's game against the Colts and head coach Dan Quinn updated their plans for his practice work at a Wednesday press conference.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Jayden Daniels made the trip to London with the Commanders for this week's game against the Colts and head coach Dan Quinn updated their plans for his practice work at a Wednesday press conference.

Daniels missed last Sunday's win over the Seahawks with the dislocated left elbow he suffered in Week 2 and Quinn said that his practice work will land him in the limited category on the team's injury report.

"Today will be more of a jog format, but if it had been a full practice it would have been limited," Quinn said.

Marcus Mariota started in Week 3 and the team will announce their starter for this week closer to Sunday's game.

Quinn said everyone with the team will participate in the job through other than running back Rachaad White, who injured his shoulder against Seattle. Guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Scott did not travel to London and will not play in the game.

item.title: PFT's Week 4 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: There's a new sheriff in town (and they're dressed like 1960s Batman).
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 2; 3-0): The Bills are No. 1, but the Adam West Batman uniforms would be No. 32.

2. Chiefs (No. 4; 3-0): The Chiefs are back . . . to playing with their food before winning easily.

3. 49ers (No. 5; 3-0): They're dropping like flies but still winning every week.

4. Broncos (No. 6; 2-1): The Rams let the Broncos hang around just long enough to steal it.

5. Jaguars (No. 7; 2-1): Get used to the possibility of seeing a lot of teal in L.A. during Super Bowl week.

6. Seahawks (No. 1; 2-1): We'll find out soon whether the loss at Washington was an aberration or a harbinger.

7. Bengals (No. 3; 2-1): You can't beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh by repeatedly shooting yourself in the foot.

8. Rams (No. 9; 1-2): With the Eagles and Bills coming up, the Rams need to flush Sunday night's outcome quickly.

9. Vikings (No. 11; 3-0): Just when it looked like they may need J.J. McCarthy at some point this season, they traded him.

10. Bears (No. 12; 2-1): They should ride with Case Keenum until Caleb Williams returns.

11. Eagles (No. 8; 2-1): Who misses A.J. Brown more? His current team or his former one?

12. Ravens (No. 13; 2-1): Great teams win games they feel destined to lose.

13. Steelers (No. 18; 2-1): There's some magic left in the post-Tomlin Steelers.

14. Lions (No. 16; 2-1): The defense still isn't nearly good enough.

15. Raiders (No. 22; 3-0): Kirk-3-and-oh Chainz.

16. Giants (No. 17; 2-1): How long will Jameis Winston hold the starting job?

17. Texans (No. 10; 0-3): The offense needed to get a little bit better. Instead, the defense got more than a little bit worse.

18. Browns (No. 23; 2-1): The Browns isn't the Browns.

19. Saints (No. 15; 1-2): It's unclear how many games they'll win, but all of them will be fun to watch.

20. Patriots (No. 14; 1-2): There was blood on the ball; now there's blood in the water.

21. Cowboys (No. 20; 1-2): How long until they can start building hype for 2027?

22. Falcons (No. 32; 1-2): Michael Penix Jr. was ready to go, just in the nick of time.

23. Commanders (No. 30; 1-2): Marcus Mariota's performance will accelerate Jayden Daniels's return.

24. Colts (No. 27; 1-2): The losing streak is over, but the Colts are still a long way from being back to what they were before last year's collapse.

25. Packers (No. 19; 1-2): The shareholders should consider a hostile takeover.

26. Panthers (No. 21; 1-2): We're learning that winning the NFC South last season doesn't mean much.

27. Cardinals (No. 24; 1-2): Reality has quickly settled in.

28. Jets (No. 28; 1-2): They'll never be a contender until they can win games they're supposed to lose.

29. Chargers (No. 25; 0-3): Justin Herbert has replaced Joe Burrow as the "veteran QB most likely to change teams in 2027."

30. Buccaneers (No. 26; 0-3): Raymond James Stadium could be Lambeau South when the Packers come to town on Sunday.

31. Titans (No. 29; 0-3): If Cam Ward is the real deal, he needs to start showing it real soon.

32. Dolphins (No. 31; 0-3): Stephen Ross won't need to offer Jeff Hafley $100,000 for each game the team loses.

item.title: More than 100 former players object to settlement of class action against NFL disability plan
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The settlement of any class action includes an opportunity for the members of the class to object to the proposed deal.
item.content:encoded:
The settlement of any class action includes an opportunity for the members of the class to object to the proposed deal. When it comes to the proposed settlement of the class action brought in 2023 against the NFL's disability plan, more than 100 former players have objected.

Via the Washington Post, the case arising from the league's use of "race-norming" has prompted the group of players (including Mike Vick, Willis McGahee, and Ricky Williams) to argue that the settlement could cost them millions in benefits.

Said former NFL defensive end Vaughn Booker in his objection to the settlement: “It’s like the defendants and counsel think non-white players are stupid. They are trying to trap us by barely giving us any notice and then telling us we cannot even opt out of the settlement.”

The ability to opt out and to pursue claims independently is usually a given in class actions. The class members then must choose whether to ride with the class, or go it alone.

Attorney Sam Katz is representing the players with objections to the deal negotiated in June.

“This settlement requires hundreds of former players to give up every legal claim they have regarding their disability benefits in exchange for essentially nothing, with no ability to opt out,” Katz told the Post.

If the contentions are accurate, it's hard to imagine the settlement being approved. Often in class actions, the lawyers representing the class become far more concerned about their fee than ensuring that justice is done for the class members. Agreeing to not allow them to opt out should be the first indication that something may be amiss.

The next hearing in the case is set for October 20.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers ties Ben Roethlisberger with 165 career wins, fifth-most ever
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: By beating the Bengals on Sunday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers equaled former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger's career win total.
item.content:encoded:
By beating the Bengals on Sunday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers equaled former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger's career win total.

Both Rodgers and Roethlisberger have exactly 165 regular-season wins as a starting quarterback, tied for the fifth-most ever. Roethlisberger played his entire career with the Steelers, while Rodgers has 147 wins with the Packers, 12 with the Steelers and six with the Jets.

The all-time record for wins by a starting quarterback may never be broken: Tom Brady retired with 251 career wins, 219 with the Patriots and 32 with the Buccaneers. You could take Rodgers' stellar career, add five 17-0 seasons on top of it, and you'd still be one win short of Brady's career win total.

Tied for second place in all-time wins are Brett Favre and Peyton Manning, each with 186. Favre won 160 starts with the Packers, 17 with the Vikings and nine with the Jets. Manning won 141 starts with the Colts and 45 with the Broncos.

Rodgers has a chance to surpass No. 4 on the all-time wins list, Drew Brees, who won 172 career games: 142 with the Saints and 30 with the Chargers. If Rodgers and the Steelers win eight more games this season, Rodgers will retire ahead of Brees and behind only Brady, Manning and Favre on the all-time wins list.

item.title: Jerry Jones: No explanation for end of Ravens loss that you're satisfied with
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.

After the team used its final timeout after a short run by quarterback Dak Prescott on second down from the 5-yard-line, they dialed up a pass play that appeared to get wide receiver George Pickens open in the end zone. Prescott threw the ball away as Pickens got free, which both he and head coach Brian Schottenheimer said was by design after the game.

During a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked about the sequence from the timing of the timeout through Prescott's throw.

“There’s no explanation that you’re satisfied with," Jones said. "None. Let’s be sure that we all understand that. They don't have one that they’re satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time, there’s no question about it. There’s no explanation. There’s an evaluation of how to not make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing. We can’t get that back. No way to get it back. What you can do is use it — if there’s any aspect of it that you want to just not even think happened. Any aspect of it, use it to get better.”

The Cowboys settled for a field goal with seven seconds left, which turned out to be just enough time for the Ravens to set up a 56-yard game-winning field goal of their own. The handling of the kickoff, which went for a touchback that took no time off the clock, was another matter lacking a satisfying rationale that might make the loss sit better with anyone.

item.title: Bengals put CB Jalen Davis on IR, sign TE Tanner Hudson to active roster
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals announced several roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals announced several roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.

They confirmed the previously reported signing of wide receiver Mitchell Tinsley off of the Texans' practice squad and that they have waived wide receiver Ke'Shawn Williams. They also placed cornerback Jalen Davis on injured reserve and signed tight end Tanner Hudson off of their practice squad.

Davis injured his hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Steelers. Davis started two of the team's three games this season and made 10 tackles. He'll have to miss at least four games before he will be able to return to the lineup.

Hudson has played in two games this year and he has three catches for 17 yards. He played in 38 games for the team over the past three seasons.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers: We had a decent offensive performance, vibes start to flow with a couple
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Steelers head into Thursday night's game against the Browns coming off their best offensive performance of the season.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers head into Thursday night's game against the Browns coming off their best offensive performance of the season.

They gained 411 yards after picking up 499 over the first two weeks and a lot of them came in big chunks through the air. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers didn't have any completions on passes that traveled 20 yards through the air in the first two weeks, but hit on two for touchdowns in the first quarter of their win over the Bengals and there were five passing plays that picked up 20-plus yards in the entire game.

On Tuesday, Rodgers said he thought the offense was "close" to what the Steelers envision it to be but noted no one felt good about the group after their Week 2 loss to New England. The goal, according to Rodgers, is to show more consistency.

"You start from zero for sure, but there's some vibes that start to flow a little bit if you put together a couple good performances in a row," Rodgers said, via the team's website. "We have one decent performance so we're gonna try and stack a few."

The Browns are coming into the game with two straight wins, but only one side is going to be able to feel like they're still on a roll once Thursday's game comes to an end.

item.title: Kevin Zeitler had a visit with the Packers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Packers have added a pair of veteran offensive linemen in the past couple of days and they may not be done addressing the area.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers have added a pair of veteran offensive linemen in the past couple of days and they may not be done addressing the area.

Tuesday's transaction report from the NFL shows that guard Kevin Zeitler visited with the team. The Wisconsin native and Wisconsin alum has been out of the league since wrapping up the 2025 season with the Titans.

Zeitler started all 16 games he played in Tennessee and has 213 career starts since entering the league as a 2012 second round pick of the Bengals.

item.title: Giants don't plan to add Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad "at this time"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The full scope of the moves the Giants made on Tuesday made their point clear.
item.content:encoded:
The full scope of the moves the Giants made on Tuesday made their point clear. They could no longer justify giving a roster spot to veteran receiver Odell Beckham Jr.

Beckham is gone, and receivers Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones have joined the 53-man roster. It's simple; Berrios and Jones play special teams. Beckham doesn't.

And it's not a simple shuffling between the roster and the practice squad. Via Jordan Raanan of ESPN, the Giants aren’t expected to sign Beckham to the practice squad "at this time."

The reunion with Beckham provided the Giants with a feel-good story, one the fans embraced. Reality has since settled in. With starting quarterback Jaxson Dart lost due to a knee injury, the Giants need to get the most out of every player on the team. Beckham wasn't doing enough. It was time for him to go.

Whether he lands elsewhere remains to be seen. Other teams, like the Rams and 49ers, have needs. More injuries are inevitable.

Last year, Beckham didn't play at all. It remains to be seen whether that will be the case for the balance of 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys have been hit hard by injuries in their secondary, which is why they had four defensive backs in town to workout.

They worked out defensive backs Juanyeh Thomas, Alex Austin, Shemar Bartholomew and Tyrek Funderburk as well as linebacker Germaine Pratt on Tuesday.

They are signing Austin, a cornerback, to the practice squad, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. They are also signing Thomas, a safety, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. It is unclear whether Thomas is signing with the active roster or the practice squad.

Austin, a seventh-round pick of the Bills in 2023, has played games for the Patriots and Texans. He has played 29 games with six starts and has 31 tackles, eight passes defensed and an interception.

Thomas signed with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He has appeared in 36 games, recording 62 tackles, five passes defensed and a forced fumble.

Cowboys safeties Malik Hooker (fractured forearm) and P.J. Locke (foot) are on injured reserve, and Jalen Thompson (hamstring) will head there this week. Cornerbacks Shavon Revel (knee/ankle) and Cobie Durant (hamstring) also are injured.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer: I hurt the team in loss to the Ravens
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said there was "no explanation" for how the team closed out the game.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer tried to explain his decisions over the final 28 seconds of Sunday's loss to the Ravens in Rio, but the guy who runs the show in Dallas made it clear on Tuesday that those explanations fell on deaf ears.

Team owner Jerry Jones said that there is "no explanation that you’re satisfied with" for how the Cowboys went from first down on the 1-yard-line to losing on a last-second field goal by Ravens kicker Tyler Loop. At a press conference later in the day, Schottenheimer said that he damaged the team's chances with his decisions over a sequence that included a timeout with 14 seconds left, coaching Dak Prescott to throw a ball away on third down rather than try to get the ball into the end zone and having Brandon Aubrey kick the ball deep after his game-tying field goal.

"I didn’t do very good in the final 28 seconds," Schottenheimer said. "When you talk about finishing the game — when you look at our two games that we’ve lost, we haven’t finished — that was a big part of this one. I felt like I overcoached Dak on third down, kinda affected his decision making a little bit. And I let that kinda bleed over to my decision about kicking the ball. . . . I’ll take accountability for it. It’s football and life, that's what happens. I hurt our chances to win that game. I’ll be better and I’m better than that."

Schottenheimer said Jones "understands there was a mistake that was made" and vowed that "those things won't happen again" in the future. He also stressed that the whole team has to be stronger in the fourth quarter if they want to avoid more painful losses in the future.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh gives Mike McDaniel a vote of confidence
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Chargers offense ranks 20th, and quarterback Justin Herbert has three touchdowns and four interceptions and his passer rating of 73.4 ranks 26th.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers offense ranks 20th, and quarterback Justin Herbert has three touchdowns and four interceptions and his passer rating of 73.4 ranks 26th. Los Angeles has more turnovers (six) than touchdowns (five) as a team.

Coach Jim Harbaugh said he has not considered taking control from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

"No, we trust Mike. We believe in Mike," Harbaugh said, via Austin Knoblauch of the Los Angeles Times.

It's not like Harbaugh has any other option but to publicly give McDaniel a vote of confidence and hope the former Dolphins head coach can fix it.

Harbaugh hired McDaniel this offseason to add a dynamic element to the offense, which hasn't happened yet.

While Harbaugh issued his first public criticism of Herbert, saying Monday that Herbert needs "to be better" in his decision-making, the head coach hasn't done the same with McDaniel.

"We're searching for every possible way to give ourselves an advantage," Harbaugh said. "Every possible way to not beat ourselves."

In his postgame comments, Herbert pushed back against the idea that McDaniel's scheme is too complex.

"He's definitely a guy that we need to lean on; he's done such an incredible job," Herbert said, via Jonah Bronstein of the Associated Press. "It's on us as an offense to run the plays the way he sees them, listen to coaching, and do our job to make those plays. And we haven't done that for him. So obviously, we feel horrible."

item.title: Jim Harbaugh: Justin Herbert needs to "be better" in his decision-making
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The coach who not long ago said Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will be remembered as the best quarterback in NFL history wants him to be better.
item.content:encoded:
The coach who not long ago said Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will be remembered as the best quarterback in NFL history wants him to be better.

Via Kris Rhim on ESPN, Jim Harbaugh offered a public critique of Herbert's decision-making to date in 2026.

"Be better," Harbaugh told reporters. "Be better. And that drives Justin, that drives me, that drives his position coach, that drives Mike [McDaniel], the [offensive] coordinator. I mean, drives us all."

With three losses in three games, Harbaugh's not wrong.

"We want to be better," Harbaugh said. "We got to be better. We got to look at our scheme. We got to look at how we're performing, how we're doing things and who's doing it."

In Sunday's loss to the Bills, which included a blown 10-0 lead, Herbert completed 20 of 34 passes for 226 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. His passer rating for the season is a career-low (by far) 73.4. (Herbert's full-season low point in passer rating is 93.2.)

Here's a theory about the current issues in L.A. With all the talk about the Oscar Madison/Felix Unger vibe between Harbaugh and McDaniel, there has been little scrutiny of the relationship between Herbert and McDaniel.

McDaniel is verbose and quirky. Herbert is quiet and no-nonsense. It's entirely possible that the personalities don't mesh, and that this has kept them from working together the way they could.

As the Chargers stare at a possible 0-6 start (they play the Seahawks, Broncos, and Chiefs before a Week 7 bye), the situation bears watching. Something's off for the Chargers' offense, and the biggest difference is that the Chargers fired offensive coordinator Greg Roman and replaced him with McDaniel.

item.title: Key pass interference decision in Rams-Broncos looked like the right call
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday night's instant classic between the Rams and Broncos had a back-to-the-future moment, when teams coached by Sean McVay and Sean Payton were involved in a potential pass interference situation with the game on the line.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday night's instant classic between the Rams and Broncos had a back-to-the-future moment, when teams coached by Sean McVay and Sean Payton were involved in a potential pass interference situation with the game on the line.

The controversial non-call from the 2018 NFC Championship between the Rams and Saints happened just outside the L.A. five yard line. The controversial call from Sunday night happened in virtually the same spot on the field.

There are different opinions about the play. Some saw interference. Some did not.

Personally, I saw interference. Rams defensive back Josh Wallace used his right hand to shove Broncos receiver Pat Bryant just before the ball arrived.

And the operative rule, which lists seven different prohibited acts by the defender when the ball is in the air, starts with this one: "Contact by a player who is not playing the ball that restricts the opponent’s opportunity to make the catch."

If the ball is arriving and the defender shoves him away from it, common sense says that was and is contact that restricts the opponent's opportunity to make the catch.

The only question is whether Wallace was "playing the ball." While on one hand he was hoping to make the interception (and did), the shove with the left hand wasn't part of the effort to make the catch. It was part of the effort to ensure that the intended receiver couldn't.

Chances are that it was a technique Wallace has learned, at some point in his time as a defensive back. A subtle, well-timed shove may not be seen by an official who is trying to sort through everything else that's happening.

Bryant, for his part, flopped after he was shoved. The SGA-level reaction, while cartoonish, doesn't change the fact that Bryant was shoved.

After the ridiculous non-call from 2018, which prompted a New Orleans boycott of Super Bowl LIII, the NFL decided to make pass interference calls and non-calls subject to replay review. The good idea was very poorly executed, and it lasted only one year.

Interference, or lack thereof, is a judgment call. Some could look at that play and see interference; others could look at the same play and reach the opposite conclusion.

That's one of the biggest problems with the former officials who take jobs in broadcasting and periodically pontificate with the benefit of a frame-by-frame, 4K monitor. The question isn't whether the former official (some of whom are former officials for a reason) subjectively believes pass interference happened. The question is whether the current official who was required to make the call in real-time with the naked eye abused his or her broad discretion.

One of the biggest problems with the TV referees is that they focus only on giving us their own interpretation of what they saw. In many cases, who cares? We all see the same thing. In those moments, those who do the job best remind us of the standard that applies to the decision that was made.

For the Broncos-Rams play, the best explanation would have been this one: "If probably wouldn't have thrown a flag if I was in that position, but there's enough there to justify someone else making a different decision."

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said this week that center Jovaugh Gwyn will be out for an extended period of time and a report on Wednesday sheds more light on the nature of his injury.

Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Gwyn fractured his fibula during last Sunday's win over the Cowboys in Rio. He is expected to miss two to three months as a result of the injury, so his return before the end of the season isn't a sure thing.

Gwyn's backup Ethan Pocic hurt his knee against the Cowboys, so rookie Vega Ioane moved over from guard to close out the game and Minter said he will remain there in Week 4.

item.title: Broncos WR Pat Bryant: I felt a nudge, sold enough to get the pass interference call
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The accuracy of the pass interference call that set the Broncos up for the winning touchdown over the Rams in last Sunday night's game has been debated around the football world, but what's not in debate is that Broncos wideout Pat Bryant did all he could to ensure a flag was thrown.
item.content:encoded:
The accuracy of the pass interference call that set the Broncos up for the winning touchdown over the Rams in last Sunday night's game has been debated around the football world, but what's not in debate is that Broncos wideout Pat Bryant did all he could to ensure a flag was thrown.

Rams defensive back Josh Wallace was covering Bryant on a pass to the sideline and Bryant did his best impression of a soccer player when he felt contact from Wallace on his back. During an interview with Romi Bean of CBS News Colorado, Bryant acknowledged that he flopped because there was a much better chance of getting a penalty than a catch on the play.

"It was a little pass interference. I did sell it just enough to get the flag," Bryant said. "He definitely gave me a little nudge that I felt. I felt like I couldn’t get the ball, so it was either the ball or the call. . . . It’s something that a lot of people do in this league, I kinda used it to my advantage."

It was a well-timed and well-executed move by Bryant that paid off handsomely when quarterback Bo Nix got into the end zone for the game-winning score a few plays later.

item.title: Greg Rousseau is first player since 1998 with 2+ sacks in first three games of a season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: While Bills quarterback Josh Allen is the leading candidate to be league MVP, his teammate linebacker Greg Rousseau is making an early case for Defensive Player of the Year.
item.content:encoded:
While Bills quarterback Josh Allen is the leading candidate to be league MVP, his teammate linebacker Greg Rousseau is making an early case for Defensive Player of the Year.

Rousseau has two sacks in each of the Bills' three games, making him just the third player since sacks became an official statistic in 1982 to have multiple sacks in the first three games of a season. The others were Mark Gastineau with the 1984 Jets and Kevin Greene with the 1998 Panthers.

Greene had multiple sacks in each of the 1998 Panthers' first four games, so Rousseau can tie Greene's record with two sacks on Sunday against the Patriots, and break the record with two sacks in each of the next two games.

Rousseau's six sacks are the most of any player in the NFL this season, and he also leads the league with eight tackles for loss and three forced fumbles. He's currently sixth in Defensive Player of the Year odds at +1500, behind Houston's Will Anderson at +300, Detroit's Aidan Hutchinson at +750, Pittsburgh's T.J. Watt at +900, Las Vegas's Maxx Crosby at +1200 and Minnesota's Dallas Turner at +1300.

item.title: Through three games, Brock Purdy still hasn't been sacked
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The 49ers are the fourth team since 1990 to allow zero sacks in their first three games.
item.content:encoded:
49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has started three games this season, thrown 83 passes, and still not been sacked.

That's a rare achievement: The 49ers are just the fourth team since 1990 to allow zero sacks through three games of a season, joining Andy Dalton with the 2014 Bengals, and Peyton Manning with the Colts in 1999 and again in 2005.

Purdy has done an excellent job this season of recognizing where the pass rush is coming from and getting rid of the ball quickly, and he has also taken off running when pressured. On 10 carries this season, Purdy has 93 rushing yards and eight first downs. Purdy is leading the league with nine touchdown passes and a 133.1 passer rating and has moved up to No. 2 in the MVP odds.

Up next for the 49ers is a game against the Broncos, who led the NFL in sacks last year and are tied for seventh in the league in sacks this year. Continuing to avoid the pass rush will be a key to Purdy's attempt to lead the 49ers to a 4-0 start.

item.title: In the offseason, Giants weren't interested in Joe Flacco
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Quarterback Joe Flacco became a free agent in March.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Joe Flacco became a free agent in March. Before re-signing with the Bengals, he explored his options.

The Giants weren't one of them.

Per a league source, Flacco had interest in the Giants. The Giants did not have interest in Flacco.

At the time, the Giants had Jameis Winston under contract through 2026. He has since signed a two-year extension.

Flacco, who played with the Ravens and current Giants coach John Harbaugh for more than a decade, eventually returned to the Bengals, on a one-year, $6 million deal. And the Bengals surely wouldn't have been willing to part with Flacco in the days since Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury; they need to have Flacco around, in the event starter Joe Burrow suffers another injury.

Still, the Giants could have had Flacco in March. While they'd never admit it, they could be privately kicking themselves that they didn't reciprocate his offseason interest.

The Giants instead will proceed with Winston, backed up by J.J. McCarthy. They surely hope Winston plays well enough to hold the job. If he doesn't, McCarthy will surely get a chance at some point.

item.title: Joe Buck hopes Troy Aikman stays at ESPN
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Joe Buck recently re-upped with ESPN.
item.content:encoded:
Joe Buck recently re-upped with ESPN. His long-time partner, Troy Aikman, is still waiting.

Buck recently said he hopes Aikman will stick around.

Appearing on 97.5 The Fanatic in Philadelphia, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing, Buck made it clear that he doesn't want to call games without Aikman in the booth.

“I’m pretty well on record, having begged out of my last years at Fox to follow him to ESPN, where I stand on all that,” Buck said. “I legitimately love the guy like a brother. We’re basically the same age; I’m 57, he’s 59. We’ve both been through divorce. We’re both girl dads. Twenty-five years, you’re sharing a lot of life together. Forget games and in the booth and all that stuff.

"So, I hope so. I mean, both of us were up. It wasn’t like we were doing some national signing day where we walk in arm-in-arm and then sign contracts at the same time. We’ve always kind of kept that stuff separate. I’m obviously hopeful, to say the least, that something gets done. But that’s kind of his world, and ESPN’s world, and I’ve got to kind of mind my own yard in that stuff. I think that’s the best way to be.”

At one point, it appeared that Buck and Aikman were a package deal. That changed, when Buck signed and Aikman didn't.

ESPN is rolling the dice by waiting. Aikman could end up at CBS or Amazon. Of course, ESPN would also have the flexibility to put the Mannings or Pat McAfee in the booth with Buck.

Then there's the white whale known as Travis Kelce. He was already sniffing around Amazon last year. He'll be able to pick his spot — and name his price — if he retires from playing after 2026.

It's also impossible to overlook the reality that Aikman's desire to double dip by working for the Dolphins and ESPN could make him less attractive. Aikman can't enter team facilities, and he can't attend practice. Others who don't work for an NFL team (or who don't partially own the team) face no such restrictions.

Aikman recently "called bullshit" on the notion that other broadcasters don't have conflicts of interest. Sorry, Troy, but you're missing the point. You work for the Dolphins, and you've said it was smart for them to take advantage of the things you learn while covering other teams. There's a very real difference between navigating friendships and owing a duty as a paid employee to a team that expects you to leverage your access to that team's benefit.

If ESPN has other options, why keep a guy who has one hand tied behind his back because he sees no issue with covering all 32 teams while working for one of them? Aikman is good, but he's not John Madden (then again, no one is). ESPN could throw money at a bigger name than Aikman, and ESPN wouldn't have to worry about the new hire having a side hustle in the form of employment by a team.

item.title: Case Keenum's Monday night performance shows importance of having three quarterbacks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Last night, Bears quarterback Case Keenum played in a regular-season game for the first time in 1,009 days.
item.content:encoded:
Last night, Bears quarterback Case Keenum played in a regular-season game for the first time in 1,009 days. He played well, and the Bears won.

The fact that the Bears had him on the roster proves the importance of having three quarterbacks who can be trusted to play, if necessary.

When the starter is injured, the team is one injury away from needing a QB3. That's what happened to the Bears. With everyone trying to figure out the extent of Caleb Williams's absence due to a hamstring injury, no one knew that Tyson Bagent (who nearly beat the Vikings in Week 2 after replacing Williams) was in the concussion protocol.

Enter Keenum. Bears coach Ben Johnson got to work on crafting a game plan based on Keenum's skills and abilities. Without Keenum, the Bears would have likely rushed to get Bagent ready, once he was cleared to play. Bagent wouldn't have been as ready as Keenum was.

It's an important aspect of roster construction to have a third quarterback who'll be able to step in effectively, if the first two are injured. Not just on game day, but in the important days preceding the game.

The teams that don't are taking a calculated risk that could lead to that one extra loss that could result in narrowly missing the playoffs once the dust settles on the regular season.

For the Bears, the Week 3 win over the Eagles becomes the difference between 1-2 and 2-1 — and the head-to-head tiebreaker with Philadelphia could become critical to figuring out the playoff tree come Week 18.
